gateway: isolated temporary home, approval=reads; a freshly seeded gateway for the stub screenshots, one for the live ones and one for the walkthrough
data: fictional, seeded through the app's HTTP API (capture/scenes.json)

agent_backend.live_model: the operator's own installed, signed-in kiro-cli over ACP with model "auto"; the replies on screen are that model's and vary from run to run
agent_backend.stub: Kiro Crew's offline stub ACP backend (capture/stub_backend.py) for every other scene; no chat reply is shown from it
agent_backend.credit_reading: the browser answers the top bar's credit readout (/api/sessions/usage) with "no reading", so no account balance or email can be shown

note: The isolated gateway served this repository's own copy of the app: capture.py's setup installed it from this checkout (POST /api/apps/install), trusted it and enabled it, so every picture shows its committed bundle (ui/dist/index.mjs) and backend. Kiro Crew still ships a built-in ops-mission-control and refuses a second install under the same name, so the Kiro Crew tree the capture ran on is the pinned commit with only the built-in copy removed (src/kiro_crew/apps/builtins/ops_mission_control and its BUILTIN_NAMES row).
data_notes: Larkspur Bikes, its services, queues and status page (status.larkspur-bikes.example) and Priya Raman are invented for this README.

The four signals arrived through the app's own signed webhook (POST /webhook with an HMAC signature over a demo signing secret); the incidents were claimed by POST /dispatch, the remembered fix was written through POST /ledger, and the transitions through POST /incident/transition.

The investigation chat slots were created the way the dispatch SOP creates them (POST /api/chat/slots), and the answer in the INV-1 chat came from a live model, so its wording differs from run to run.
Incident ages ("36s") are real: the board was photographed seconds after seeding.
